Consider the graph of the function $f(x),$ shown above. It consists of an arc of a quarter-circle centered at $(-1,0)$ with radius $2$, an arc of a semi-circle centered at $(0,2)$ with radius $1$, and an arc of a quarter-circle centered at $(1,0)$ with radius $2.$ Find the value of ${\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$

${\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The graph consists of $3$ parts: the arc of a quarter-circle for $x\in [-3,-1]$, the arc of a semi-circle for $x\in [-1,1]$, and the arc of a quarter-circle for $x\in [1,3].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,-1].$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,1].$ The corresponding region is a combination of a semi-circle and a square, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2}+{a}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot {1}^{2}+{2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,3].$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle centred at $(1,0),$ so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{2}+4+\pi  \\  & =4+\frac{5\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
